text:
maria: Hey team — after rebasing feature/stream-cache-rework onto main I’m seeing CI red on the integration shard. Can someone eyeball? https://buildkite.com/redwood/infra/builds/4523 :grimacing:

ci-bot: Build #4523 — shard: integration-12 — failed
• step: integration-tests (linux) — exit code 1
• failing test: TestKVCacheEvicts

maria: dump from test run attached below, looks like a timing assertion during eviction:
```
--- FAIL: TestKVCacheEvicts (0.23s)
    cache_test.go:142: expected 1 evictions, got 0
    kv_cache.go:87: last_inserted_key=abc123, last_evicted_key=
```

tony: I can take a look. Did you rebase any cache invalidation code or change default TTLs?

maria: I rebased and resolved a conflict in runtime/kv_cache.go — mostly import ordering and a small tweak to eviction callback. I didn't touch TTLs.

jen: Quick question: can you rerun just the failing shard? sometimes flakies are transient.

maria: kicked off a rerun: https://buildkite.com/redwood/infra/builds/4523#rebuild-2

ci-bot: Rebuild triggered by maria — integration-12 queued

sam: rerun passed?

ci-bot: Rebuild #4523.2 — integration-12 — still failing (same test)

lukas: can you run a local unit-only run for that test with `-run TestKVCacheEvicts -count 10` to check flakiness?

maria: running locally now, 10 runs, 0/10 failures so far. Strange.

tony: that suggests it may be infra-related (timing under CI) OR a subtle reorder introduced by the rebase. Two quick things: 1) bisect to narrow commit, 2) dump the evict logs with extra debug.

maria: starting a bisect on the feature branch between upstream/main@d4f2 and my branch tip. Will run `git bisect run ./scripts/ci-bisect.sh` which executes the test in CI environment.

jen: ping me if bisect lands on a merge commit — I can help interpret. Also add `-race` if possible to catch concurrency issues.

maria: bisect log (short):
```
bisect start d4f2..feature/stream-cache-rework
good d4f2
bad feature-tip
# automated run: commit 7a1c6 -> test failed (integration-12)
# automated run: commit e13bd -> test passed
# automated run: commit 4c9ab -> test failed
# first bad commit: 4c9ab (Merge: 2f3b 9a5d)
```

maria: so it points at merge commit 4c9ab where I resolved conflicts.

tony: can you paste the conflict resolution hunk from kv_cache.go around the eviction callback?

maria: here's the snippet I used in the merge resolution:
```
-    // old behavior: synchronous eviction call
-    evictCb := func(k Key) { handleEvict(k) }
+    // merged change: use goroutine to avoid blocking main insert path
+    evictCb := func(k Key) { go handleEvict(k) }
```

lukas: ah — that is likely the culprit. Converting the eviction callback to async can make the eviction not happen before the test assertion. Tests expect synchronous eviction.

jen: two immediate fixes: revert to synchronous behavior for now, or update the test to poll/wait for eviction (less ideal).

maria: I pushed a quick patch to make eviction synchronous again in the merge commit resolution: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/7892 — running CI now.

ci-bot: Build triggered for PR #7892 — integration-12 queued

ci-bot: PR #7892 — integration-12 — passed ✅

maria: Thanks all! Rebase + conflict resolution introduced an async eviction change that flaked the test. I updated the merge resolution to preserve sync behavior. Will follow up with a separate PR to make the eviction behavior explicit and add a test that tolerates async behavior if we want to change it globally. :slightly_smiling_face:

tony: great triage. Recommend adding a comment near the callback explaining test expectations.

maria: will do. Closing the thread once CI merges. :white_check_mark:
